newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends firmer after choppy session.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends firmer after choppy session.

text.p: COMEX copper settled firmer after a choppy session in a market that lacked conviction and volume as to which direction to take, traders said.
A dip of 3,050 tonnes in LME stocks to 205,525 tonnes was only mildly supportive because it was in line with trader expectations.
"I am not sure it's going to start going to the highs again, but it did come back off the lows and support held," a trader said.
The arbitrage on spot March to LME cash has widened to about 5 cents, more than enough to attract metal from LME warehouses in the U.S. to COMEX depots, if it is available, a trader said.
The COMEX May premium over LME May contract also widened slightly to about 2 cents by close of trade in New York.
May COMEX settled 0.70 cent firmer at 110.65 cents a lb, traded 111.40 to 108.80 cents. Spot March went out 0.45 cent higher at 115.10 cents.

Traders have said that good Chinese buying was probably needed to help copper break through upside resistance, but reports earlier this week quoted Chinese traders saying copper was currently too expensive.
Copper is supported by low stock levels, but unable to make further upside progress, and is therefore left to drift in a range for the time being, traders said.
